property_summary: For any implementation of ERC721TokenReceiver, onERC721Received must return the selector 0x150b7a02, but the mutant returns 0x01ffc9a7 instead.

After initialization, the stored feeRate must equal the input _feeRate if and only if _feeRate <= 5000, otherwise the call must revert without storing the value; the buggy version stores the excessive feeRate before the revert, leaving a non-zero feeRate.
After initialization reverts due to a feeRate > 5000, the reference contract always has feeRate == 0, but the buggy version may have feeRate > 0 because it stores the value before the revert check.
After a call to initialize() fails due to excessive _feeRate, the reference contract's stored feeRate remains 0, while the buggy contract incorrectly leaves the excessive value stored.

After a successful initialize call, feeRate must equal the _feeRate argument; the mutant satisfies this for all calls that succeed, while the reference also does, so the difference only appears when _feeRate > 5000 and the call reverts, preventing initialization, but the mutant stores the feeRate before reverting. Therefore, after a failed initialize due to excessive feeRate, the reference feeRate remains 0, while the mutant feeRate equals the excessive input.
After initialize reverts with FeeRateTooHigh, feeRate must remain 0; the mutant stores the excessive feeRate before reverting, so feeRate equals the input > 5000 instead.
